title: WASiM Model (Primitives)
description: Canonical model definition for a probabilistic, dynamic (Monte-Carlo) simulation. Built on six composable primitives (node, stock, link, event, gate, cell) with behavior determined by field presence (traits) rather than a fixed type taxonomy. Vendor-neutral. See wasim-engine-semantics.md for behavioral contracts.

source.description: Provenance metadata. Not consumed by the engine.

optimization.description: Optional study-level optimization config (search for input values that make a result best). Absent for non-optimization models. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §13.

dimensions.description: Ordinal-set declarations — named, ordered dimensions (e.g. Months = 12 members) that `vector_map` comprehensions iterate over and `output_spec.dimensions` reference. Empty for scalar-only models. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §15.

elements.description: Flat list of all model elements. Hierarchy via container references. Every element `id` MUST be globally unique across this list (see element_base.id and wasim-engine-semantics.md §1); string references resolve by exact id, not by scoped name.

connections.description: Visual connection graph from source model. Not consumed by the engine; preserved for rendering.

time_history_displays.description: Display-only expressions recovered from result/plot elements. Not part of the simulation graph.

simulation_settings.description: Time-stepping and Monte-Carlo controls. A `duration` of 0 denotes a single-evaluation (driver/instant) model: the engine evaluates the model once at t=start and stops (see wasim-engine-semantics.md §9). `duration` must be >= 0; `timestep` must be > 0.

calendar_start.description: Model-clock start as seconds since the Unix epoch (B6). When set, time_ref calendar properties use a real proleptic-Gregorian calendar with leap years. Absent = fixed 365-day calendar.

kind.description: Structural role. 'container'/'group': purely organizational (the engine ignores them). 'submodel': a nested simulation that runs with its own clock/sampling controls (see simulation_settings) and exposes a named interface. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §12.

simulation_settings.description: For kind='submodel': the nested run's time-stepping / Monte-Carlo settings. Null (or absent) inherits the parent model's settings.

interface.description: Named inputs/outputs exposed at the container boundary (for submodels). See wasim-engine-semantics.md §12.

inputs.description: Boundary inputs: each binds a parent driver element to an interior consumer element.

input.description: Full slash-path id of the interior element the value flows into (the consumer).

from.description: Full slash-path id of the parent element that drives it. Null for an engine/dashboard-supplied input with no model driver (e.g. realization count).

outputs.description: Full slash-path ids of interior elements exposed as boundary outputs.

optimization.description: For kind='submodel' only: a dynamic (per-timestep) optimization. The inner search is re-solved at each outer timestep against the objective evaluated at that step, so the optimized variables become per-timestep series rather than a single study result. Objective/variable element ids are interior submodel elements. Absent = the submodel is not optimized. Distinct from the top-level `optimization` block, which is a once-only study. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §13a.

dimension_def.description: A named, ordered dimension (ordinal set). `size` members, optionally labeled. `vector_map.over` and `output_spec.dimensions` reference these by `id`.

labels.description: Optional member labels in order (e.g. Jan..Dec). If present, length should equal `size`. Member numeric values, if any, live in the element that carries them, indexed by position.

quantity_or_formula.description: A value that may be a fixed quantity, a parsed expression AST, or an unparsed formula string (fallback).

oneOf.description: Unparsed formula (fallback). Engines should treat as 0.0 and warn.

quantity_expr.description: A value that may be a fixed quantity or an expression AST.

optimization.description: Study-level optimization: search input values (variables) that make a result (objective) best. The problem definition only; the solver (e.g. Box's complex method) is an engine concern, not schema. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §13.

element_id.description: Id of the result element being optimized. Must depend on every optimization variable.

statistic.description: [probabilistic] the Monte-Carlo statistic of the objective output reduced across realizations; null (or absent) means a deterministic objective.

p.description: Percentile in [0,100]. Required when kind='percentile'; ignored otherwise.

variables.description: The input elements the optimizer may adjust. Each references an editable fixed-value or sample element, with SI bounds + initial guess.

integer.description: Restrict the search to integer values.

constraints.description: Optional conditions a valid solution must satisfy.

sampling.description: [probabilistic] Monte-Carlo runs per candidate solution; null (or absent) if deterministic. When the objective references a submodel, this may be null and the submodel's own simulation_settings.n_realizations governs.

dimensions.description: Ids of the dimensions (top-level `dimensions[]`) this output is dimensioned over. Empty = scalar.

role.description: The flow a stock's secondary output port reports (semantics §1c). 0.9.7 splits the flow identity from its accumulation: `role` names the flow ({addition, withdrawal, overflow, net_change}) and `output_kind` says how it accumulates. The fused `*_rate` names are retained as 0.9.6 aliases, each equivalent to `<flow>` with `output_kind: rate`. Role-less secondaries resolve to the element's primary value.

output_kind.description: How this output accumulates the flow named by `role` (semantics §1c). `level` = the stock's own value (its primary output); `rate` = the per-step applied flow (units = value/time); `cumulative` = the running total of that flow since the run start (units = value). Absent on a plain result output. When `role` is a flow name, `output_kind` disambiguates rate vs cumulative; when absent it defaults to `rate` (0.9.6 back-compat, where reservoir/pool roles were all rates).

oneOf.description: Numeric literal.
Reference to another element's output.
Simulation time property.
Binary operation.
Unary operation.
Built-in function call.
Inline array constructor.
Conditional (if/then/else).
Lookup table evaluation.
A Monte-Carlo statistic of a submodel output, reduced across the submodel's realizations (the `pdf_*` operations). See wasim-engine-semantics.md §2 and SUBMODEL_STAT_ENCODING.md.

submodel_id.description: Full slash-path id of the submodel container.

output.description: Full slash-path id of the interface output element being reduced.

arg.description: Required for `percentile` (p in [0,100]), `cumulative_prob`/`exceedance` (threshold value, may carry a unit) and `cte` (percentile); omitted for `mean`/`sd`/`sum`/`min`/`max`.

oneOf.description: Comprehension over an ordinal set: evaluate `body` (which may reference `index_ref`) once per member of the dimension `over`, producing an array dimensioned over that set. A matrix is nested `vector_map`s. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §15.

over.description: Id of the dimension (top-level `dimensions[]`) the result is dimensioned over.

oneOf.description: The implicit iteration index inside a `vector_map` body. `row` is the first (array) axis; `col` the matrix second axis.

depth.description: Read the iteration index of the n-th enclosing `vector_map` (0 = innermost, equivalent to axis `row`; 1 = `col`). Generalizes `axis` past two dimensions for ≥3-D arrays. When present, overrides `axis`.

oneOf.description: Array/matrix element access: array[i] or matrix[i, j]. `indices` holds one expression for a vector access or two for a matrix access (indices may be `index_ref`s).

A source-model function the engine does not implement. Preserves the call (name + args) for round-tripping and connectivity; the engine treats it as opaque (evaluates to 0.0 with a warning). Use `call` for functions in the implemented `fn` enum; use `extern_call` for everything else so argument refs are still preserved.
Bivariate reduction of two outputs of the SAME submodel across that submodel's realizations — the `submodel_stat` analog of `run_stat2` (cov/corr/beta). See CONTROL_VARIATE_SCOPE.md Phase 4.

Conditional nested-submodel statistic: for each OUTER realization the submodel is re-run with its input constants bound to this path's realized values (`bindings`), and `statistic` reduces the inner `output`'s per-inner-realization finals. See NESTED_STAT_SCOPE.md.

arg.description: Literal argument for arg-taking statistics (percentile level, threshold, …).

bindings.description: Pin inner input constants to outer elements' per-realization values (what makes the inner run conditional on the outer state).

each_step.description: false (default): bind to each outer realization's terminal state. true: bind at every timestep (per-step conditional expectation; exposure profiles, PFE).

oneOf.description: Label subscript: select the slice of `array` where dimension `dim` equals `label` (Analytica `x[Dim = 'label']`). See WASIM_NAMEDARRAY_DESIGN.md §4.

Across-realization reduction of a same-model element over the Monte-Carlo Run axis (Analytica `Mean(x)`, `Probability(x>t)`). Pre-computed by the engine's two-pass driver; no topo dependency on `element_id`. See WASIM_NAMEDARRAY_DESIGN.md §4.

arg.description: Required by percentile / cumulative_prob / exceedance / cte.

oneOf.description: Bivariate across-realization reduction of two same-model elements over the Monte-Carlo Run axis — the cov/corr/regression-slope companion to `run_stat`. `beta` = Cov(x,y)/Var(x). See CONTROL_VARIATE_SCOPE.md.
Multiple-control regression: the `index`-th OLS slope coefficient of regressing `y` on `controls` across realizations (control-variate generalization). See CONTROL_VARIATE_SCOPE.md Phase 3.

Split-sample (K-fold jackknife) control-variate coefficient — a per-realization reduction. For realization i, beta(x,y) estimated over every realization NOT in i's fold. See CONTROL_VARIATE_SCOPE.md Phase 3.

Longstaff-Schwartz least-squares Monte Carlo for an early-exercise (American / Bermudan) option. Evaluates to this realization's discounted-to-t0 cashflow, so the element's mean is the option price. See AMERICAN_OPTION_SCOPE.md.

state.description: Element whose per-step history is the regression state (usually the underlying price).

states.description: Additional state elements for a multi-asset early-exercise option (multivariate monomial basis, total degree ≤ basis). Empty (default) = single-asset.

payoff.description: Element whose per-step history is the immediate-exercise payoff.

basis.description: Polynomial basis degree in the (scaled) state; default 3.

rate.description: Annual risk-free rate for per-step discounting.

folds.description: Cross-fit folds. 1 (default) = in-sample; ≥ 2 = out-of-sample k-fold cross-fit.

oneOf.description: Dual (upper-bound) companion to `lsm`. With `inner`=0 the loose single-hedge dual; with `inner`>0 the tight nested-Doob dual. Evaluates to this realization's max_t(Z_t - M_t), so the mean is the dual price. See AMERICAN_OPTION_SCOPE.md §8.

rate.description: Annual risk-free rate for per-step discounting.

inner.description: Inner samples for the tight (nested Doob) dual. 0 (default) = the loose single-hedge dual.

importance.description: Importance-sampling override (semantics § importance sampling). When present, the engine draws from `bias` (the biased distribution g) instead of this declared distribution (the target f), and weights every statistic by the likelihood ratio f(x)/g(x) — a variance-reduction technique for rare events. Phase 1 supports `bias` families {normal, lognormal, uniform, exponential} (a closed-form PDF is required for both f and g); other families error. An importance node draws plain Monte Carlo (LHS stratification / rank-correlation are skipped for that node).

bias.description: The biased distribution g to sample from. Same schema as any distribution.

mean.description: Drift (per-time rate). Interpreted per `mean_type`. May be reference/formula-valued.

reversion_rate.description: Mean-reversion rate (per-time). Absent or zero = a non-reverting random walk (plain GBM/arithmetic). Non-zero makes the process mean-revert toward `reference_value` at this rate (an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-style pull). May be reference/formula-valued. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §16.

reference_value.description: The long-run level the process reverts toward when `reversion_rate` is non-zero. Required for a meaningful reversion; ignored when reversion is absent/zero. May be reference/formula-valued.

initial_value.description: The process value at t=0. Absent = start from the reference/drift-implied level. May be reference/formula-valued (e.g. an array-comprehension for a correlated array process); the engine resolves only the scalar form today.

species.description: Species-element id transported by this flux (per (species, medium) pair). id, not raw label.

medium.description: Medium-element id the flux moves the species through. id, not raw label.

source.description: Upstream cell id. On a cell.fluxes[] entry, absent = the owning cell (implicit source). On a link, the link's source.

payoff_spec.description: A financial payoff carried by an event (§19): an option (pays when the underlying crosses the strike) or insurance (pays claims above a deductible up to a coverage cap). Element-id fields reference the driving inputs. Provenance-complete; the engine does not yet execute payoffs.

strike_input.description: [option] Element id of the strike price.

maturity_input.description: [option] Element id of the maturity/exercise time.

underlying_input.description: [option] Element id of the underlying value.

deductible_input.description: [insurance] Element id of the per-claim deductible.

coverage_limit_input.description: [insurance] Element id of the coverage cap.

transition_entry.description: One row of a Markov transition matrix, or an expression-valued entry.

oneOf.description: Fixed probability row (must sum to 1).
Expression-valued probability row.

id.description: Globally-unique element handle. MUST be unique across every element in `elements` (not merely within a container). All string references — `inputs[]`, AST `ref`/`lookup_call` `element_id`, `container.elements[]`, `container.interface`, and `optimization` element ids — resolve to this exact id by string equality; there is no relative-name or scope-aware resolution. Source names are container-scoped and collide, so emitters use a scope-qualified id (e.g. a path like `Model/CoverLayer/nCells`). JSON Schema does not enforce this uniqueness; it is a contract engines rely on. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §1.

name.description: Human-readable display name (may collide across containers; not a reference key — use `id`).

inputs.description: Ids of elements this element depends on. Each entry MUST equal a target element's `id` exactly (§1 identity rule); a reference that matches no id is dangling and the engine evaluates it as 0.0 with a warning.

source_type.description: Original element type from source model. Engine ignores.

oneOf.description: NODE: Produces a value at each timestep. Discriminated by 'value_rule'.

unit.description: [fixed array] Shared unit for array values.

cells.description: [spreadsheet] The element's linked-Excel I/O cells: each binds a model port to a workbook range. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §20. The engine does not evaluate spreadsheet links (the workbook is external); this carries the binding for round-trip and inspection.

direction.description: input = a model value written into the workbook; output = a workbook value read into the model.

range.description: The Excel range reference (e.g. 'WGEN Parameters!B5' or 'Observed Stats!B7:B18').

port.description: The bound model port/element id (the consumer for output cells, the source for input cells).

external_file.description: [spreadsheet] Path/reference of the linked workbook, when available.

calendar_based.description: [series] True when the source series was calendar-dated. Its `timestamps` are re-based to elapsed-from-sim-start (starting at 0); `calendar_start_seconds` recovers the absolute axis. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §18.

calendar_start_seconds.description: [series] For a calendar-based series: the absolute epoch time (seconds) of timestamp 0, so `absolute = calendar_start_seconds + timestamps[i]`. Null/absent for an elapsed-native series.

n_histories.description: [series] When the source stored a stochastic ensemble of realization histories, the number carried. `values`/`timestamps` are the first history; the rest are not (yet) represented. 1 (or absent) = a single deterministic history.

extra_value_rows.description: [series] Additional value rows for a multi-column (array-valued) series; each row aligns with `timestamps`. Empty/absent for a scalar series.

input.description: [lag, convolution, hysteresis, filter] Element id of the input signal.

oneOf.description: Element id of a lookup/series supplying the response function.

An expression-valued response: a formula over the local lag variable (an `extern_call` `fn: "lag"` node, τ ≥ 0), sampled by the engine onto the lag grid at run time. Unlike the baked `{times, values}` form, this keeps any referenced parameter live — so a calibratable unit hydrograph (e.g. GR4J `IF(lag < X4, (lag/X4)^2.5, 1)`, X4 an optimization variable) responds to the parameter rather than a value frozen at emit time. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §17.

expression.description: The response formula over the lag variable.

cumulative.description: When true the expression is a cumulative response (an S-curve); the convolution weights are its successive differences. When false it is a density; weights = value × interval.

transition_matrix.description: [markov] Row-stochastic transition matrix. Rows sum to 1.

window.description: [filter] Window size in timesteps (or EMA span).

root.description: [gate_logic] Root of the boolean logic tree.

setpoint.description: [pid] Target value the controller drives `input` toward.

deadband.description: [pid] Error magnitude treated as zero (anti-chatter), as a number.

controller_mode.description: [pid] GoldSim controller mode (semantics §2.15). `pid` (default) / `proportional` (kp only) use the PID law; `on_off` is a stateful bang-bang hysteresis latch (ON above setpoint+band/2, OFF below setpoint−band/2, else HOLD).

output_cap.description: [pid on_off] The "ON" output value of an on_off controller (may be a dynamic ref). Absent → the latch emits a 0/1 gate signal.

deadband_ref.description: [pid on_off] The on_off hysteresis band as a quantity_or_formula (distinct from the numeric `deadband`); supersedes `deadband` for on_off when present.

delay_time.description: [queue] Fixed transit/service delay for a `queue` value_rule node (required for queue nodes).

leak_rate.description: [queue] Optional first-order decay applied over a queue node's transit (a scheduled parcel of size `a` with transit `T` exits as `a·exp(-leak_rate·T)`); models loss/reneging in transit. Mirrors link `decay_rate`.

discipline.description: [queue] Delay-sampling discipline. `conveyor` (default) = fixed transit from entry (plug flow). `fixed_at_entry` = delay sampled once when the entity is admitted. Equivalent under a constant `delay_time`.

oneOf.description: STOCK: State variable that accumulates over time. Traits activated by field presence.

initial_value.description: The stock's level at t=0. A scalar quantity, or an expression over other elements (including other stocks' initials — resolved by an init-only topological order at t=0; a circular initial dependency falls back to the scalar/0 seed with a warning).

inflows.description: Element ids contributing to positive rate.

outflows.description: Element ids contributing to negative rate.

overflow_target.description: TRAIT: overflow_routing. Element id receiving excess. Requires capacity.

oneOf.description: LINK: Directed connection moving quantity from source to target.

source.description: Element id of the upstream stock/cell.

target.description: Element id of the downstream stock/cell.

fraction.description: Transfer as fraction of source output.

decay_rate.description: TRAIT: transit_decay. First-order loss in transit. Requires transit_time.

dispersion.description: TRAIT: transit_dispersion. Péclet number (dimensionless, unit '1'). Higher = less dispersion. Requires transit_time. Math spec deferred to M4 appendix.

oneOf.description: EVENT: Discrete occurrence that fires on a trigger and applies effects.

count_limit.description: Maximum number of events over the run.

rate.description: TRAIT: rate_generation. Mean Poisson event rate.

failure_process.description: TRAIT: failure_state_machine. How the component fails and is repaired.

payoff.description: TRAIT: financial payoff (option/insurance). A threshold-conditional payout that ordinary `effects` (additive/multiplicative/replace) can't express. Provenance-complete; engine execution is deferred. See wasim-engine-semantics.md §19.

oneOf.description: GATE: Boolean logic composition (fault tree, RBD, event tree).
CELL: Transport compartment holding species across media.

release_target.description: TRAIT: source_release. Cell receiving released mass.

fluxes.description: TRAIT: coupled_transport. Advective/diffusive inter-cell mass transfer. Each entry is cell-owned: `source` absent = this cell, `target` = the far cell. Advective reads `rate` (volumetric flow); diffusive reads `coefficient`.

oneOf.description: SPECIES: Definition of a transported substance (no simulation behavior).

members.description: Per-nuclide decay data when this element is a species SET (GoldSim SSpeciesElem: N nuclides as one dimension element). Cells and `decay_products[].species` reference members by bare `name`, not the set element id; the engine keys its per-nuclide decay table by member name. Empty for a plain single-species element.

name.description: Nuclide label, unique within the set. Referenced by cells and by other members' decay_products.

species.description: Daughter member name (resolved within this set's membership).

oneOf.description: MEDIUM: Definition of a material phase (no simulation behavior).
